picks.blurb: Minnesota-UCLA score predictions from Bring Me The Sports staff - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB March Madness Week 9 Winners and Losers Bears beat Bucs, barely Lakers win without Luka Puka Nacua needs MRI Minnesota-UCLA score predictions from Bring Me The Sports staff Tony Liebert · BringMeTheSports Fri, November 6, 2026 at 10:43 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Gophers have a golden opportunity for their third field storming of the season this week when No. 8 UCLA comes to town. The Bruins are 8-0 this season and one of the best stories in the sport under first-year head coach Bob Chesney. Can Minnesota stop their momentum? Here are our staff writers' predictions. Tony Liebert: Minnesota 21, UCLA 14 P.J. Fleck has a track record of performing well as a home underdog, and he has a great chance to add to that narrative this week against UCLA. The Bruins haven't played on the road since sneaking past Oregon for their best win on Oct. 10. The only thing that scares me for the Gophers' chances this week is a hangover after last week's emotional loss to Indiana, but I expect Fleck's team to be ready to end UCLA's perfect season. Joe Nelson: Minnesota 21, UCLA 17 I don't want to say UCLA doesn't deserve to be ranked in the top 10, but who have they actually beaten to prove they're legit? Oregon without Dante Moore? Please. Every team gives the Ducks a run for their money this year. Wisconsin's a fraud; Purdue can't play defense; Michigan State, Nevada, Maryland, San Diego State and Cal all stink. As long as Minnesota doesn't get gashed on the ground, they're going to limit Ty Dieffenbach through the air. Dieffenbach can't move (kinda like Mr. Statue Drake Lindsey), and that's bad news for the Bruins, who will go home with an 8-1 record Will Ragatz: Minnesota 20, UCLA 17 Since getting embarrassed by Purdue, the Gophers have upset Iowa and come oh-so-close to doing the same to Indiana. They've done it by dragging those ranked teams into low-scoring slugfests. Can they do it to undefeated UCLA this week? I'm inclined to think they can. Outside of Oregon and maybe Wisconsin, the Bruins haven't exactly beaten anyone notable. Backup QB Ty Dieffenbach is still fairly inexperienced. And UCLA is coming to Minneapolis to play in 40-degree temps in a game that kicks off at 9 a.m. Pacific time. This will be another big win and field storm for P.J. Fleck. Jonathan Harrison: Minnesota 18, UCLA 15 On the road last week, the Gophers surprised everybody and took the defending champs to overtime. Despite an offense that can't seem to get going, Minnesota has hung around in most games. I think we'll see something similar with the Gophers' defense limiting a UCLA offense that is somehow averaging fewer passing yards than Minnesota this season. The Bruins have a top-15 run game, though, so Minnesota's defense will have its hands full there. This is going to be the question going forward: until proven otherwise, can the Gophers' offense do just enough to squeak out a win? I'm predicting that, with the home crowd behind them, that's the case on Saturday. Here are our picks from last week . The Bruins were No. 8 in the first round of College Football Playoff rankings, which doesn't matter. If they end up 10-2, as a Big Ten team, they're a mortal lock to get into the CFP. But at this point, they want a spot in the Big Ten Championship, and they're good enough to beat anyone left on the slate. Minnesota has proven it's almost good enough to beat anyone, losing a brutal 23-16 heartbreaker to Indiana last week. It beat Iowa and Michigan, but a weird 41-13 loss at Purdue is an issue for an at-large CFP spot. However, win out, and there's a shot at getting into the Big Ten title game. UCLA vs Minnesota: Quick Hits UCLA gets Illinois in the Rose Bowl next, then has to travel to Michigan, and finishes up down the road at USC. Minnesota goes to Penn State next week, hosts Northwestern, and close with the Paul Bunyan Axe game at Wisconsin. The two programs have only faced each other four times, with Minnesota winning the last meeting 21-17 in 2024. The Gophers are 3-1, starting with a 21-3 win in the 19162 Rose Bowl. How To Watch UCLA vs Minnesota Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis, MN – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why UCLA Will Win Run, run, and keep running. There's no real mystery to what UCLA does. It blasts away, with the ground game, gets just enough from the passing game to get by, and then it relies on the defense to take care of everything else. It starts with third down stops. Only Nebraska – at least before the loss to Illinois – is better at defensively on third downs than the Bruins. That allows UCLA to dominate the time of possession battle, the rested defense forces a ton of takeaways, the offense capitalizes … repeat. However … Why Minnesota Will Win UCLA runs well, Minnesota doesn't. Minnesota can throw well, UCLA doesn't. Other than that, these two do almost all of the same things. You want third down defense? Minnesota is sixth in the nation, allowing teams to convert just 28% of their chances. Time of possession? The Gophers aren't as good as UCLA, but they're fine, usually keeping the ball for close to 32 minutes per game. And then there are the takeaways – Minnesota is good at that, too. UCLA vs Minnesota Prediction, Betting Lines The whole Big Noon Kickoff aspect to this is a problem for UCLA. The Bruins have to be ready to rumble at 9:00 am Los Angeles time. And then there's the other issue. When the ball gets kicked off in Minneapolis, it will be around 71 degrees in LA. The temperature should hover around 40 degrees and feel more like 32ish for the entire game in Huntington Bank. UCLA will be pushed and tested, and Minnesota will take advantage of that early, but the score will be kept low throughout, and the Bruins will still be alive in the second half, when the ground game starts to take over. It'll be another tremendously entertaining Minnesota game to kick off a whale of a Saturday. This Week’s Thoughts: GopherNation: I feel strongly that this is a win for P.J. Fleck and the Gophers. UCLA’s only trip outside of their time zone was a trip to Maryland and I can safely say that Minnesota is much better than the Terps. I think Minnesota still sucks on offense, but they beat the Bruins. Andy York : Going full reverse jinx here. I do think the Gophers can win this game if they can continue to play amazing defense and special teams and get just ANYTHING out of the offense. But this UCLA defense is really good. And Wayne Knight is really good. We have done a good job against power running teams this season and will need to do so again. But its definitely going to be close. Blake Ruane : See my opponent preview. Ustreet: Rock fight again. zipsofakron : UCLA at #5 (in the AP Top 25) is a travesty and I’m betting on Minnesota to be hot after a narrow miss in Bloomington. Hoping that Greg Harbaugh and Drake Lindsey took a long look in the mirror this week and will move away from running screens that regularly lose yards. Unlikely, I know, but a guy can hope! mowe0018: While I believe UCLA to be slightly above trash, until P.J. changes his approach and in-game philosophy, the team will not be successful against talented teams. wildcat00: I don’t have a good feeling about this one. I’m also still super upset about the last game, and I suspect the team is, too. WhiteSpeedReceiver: This doesn’t feel like a game that’ll go well for UCLA. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 5 Alabama is out to defend its College Football Playoff ranking, while No. 14 LSU seeks to remain in the hunt Getty Images One of the best modern-day rivalries in college football headlines on Saturday when No. 5 Alabama and No. 14 LSU meet in Baton Rouge for the 91st meeting in the series. The Crimson Tide hold a 58-27-5 advantage overall, but it's the 13-2 record in the past 15 meetings that has given them the upper hand in a battle between programs that would otherwise be considered peers. This is, after all, set to be the 25th time that both schools are inside the top 15 of the AP Top 25 poll and with Alabama's recent crowning as a top-five team in the College Football Playoff rankings, there's even more ranked-on-ranked intrigue. LSU is hoping that the home field advantage of Death Valley can play a role in the game, as the Tigers are 32-3 in their last 35 home games in Tiger Stadium. Speaking of streaks, the game also presents LSU coach Lane Kiffin with a chance to finally defeat Alabama as a head coach. The former Crimson Tide offensive coordinator lost to Nick Saban once as Tennessee's head coach in 2009, then four times between 2020-23 as Ole Miss ' head coach, when they were SEC West division rivals. That 0-5 record against the Crimson Tide, paired with LSU's recent struggles in the series, provides plenty of extra motivation for the home team looking to roar back into the playoff race. Where to watch Alabama vs. LSU live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Tiger Stadium -- Baton Rouge, Louisiana TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Alabama vs. LSU: Need to know Alabama's injury report will be an X-factor: There will be key updates throughout the week, perhaps all the way up to warm-ups, that will determine the health of the Crimson Tide and their ability to perform to the expectations of their top-five rating. Starting center Racin Delgatty has missed multiple games while dealing with injury, and his absence has been noticeable on an offensive line that has cooled off since putting up 49+ points in consecutive wins against Florida State , South Carolina and Mississippi State . The Crimson Tide have failed to record 70+ rushing yards as a team in each of their last two games and allowed 21 sacks in SEC play, which ranks 14th among 16 teams in the league. Alabama will also be looking for updates from star wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams and cornerback Zabien Brown , adding to the unknowns for how the Tide will stack up against LSU. LSU passing attack rounding into form : No one in the SEC had a more productive passing attack in the month of October than LSU, which averaged 339.5 passing yards across all four games last month. The Tigers went 3-1 across those games, only losing to top-10 Kentucky by one point in Lexington on a walk-off two-point try. LSU now leads the SEC and ranks tied for 7th nationally on the season, averaging 318.0 passing yards per game, and the improvements have come with both Sam Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris as a go-to receiver. A transfer from Hawaii , Harris played three whole games before scoring his first touchdown of the season but has exploded ever since with seven touchdown catches across the last five games. That includes four multiple-touchdown games and a yards-per-reception average (17.6) that ranks 4th among all SEC pass catchers. Kalen DeBoer set up in some favorable situational spots : When Alabama hired Kalen DeBoer away from Washington to take over in Tuscaloosa after Nick Saban's retirement, his track record as a big-time, high-leverage coach met the demands of the job. Since Alabama is almost always playing in high-pressure games against quality opponents, the school needed to know that Saban's successor would be ready for those moments. Currently, DeBoer is 21-8 against AP-ranked teams as a head coach, which is the fourth-best record in AP poll history with a minimum of 20 games coached (.724 winning percentage). His company on that list, for those unaware, is one spot behind Urban Meyer (.746) and one spot ahead of Kirby Smart (.710). DeBoer has also won eight straight games after a bye, with the last defeat in this spot coming in 2020 as the head coach of Fresno State . Alabama vs. LSU prediction, picks While the combination of LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt and Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell provides the potential for plenty of points, this game could end up being decided by both defenses. Alabama's offensive injuries have clearly limited their ability to execute on schedule, and LSU's defense represents the best test they've faced since the loss at Tennessee. In the same manner, LSU's pass attack could set them up for some of the turnovers that have powered Alabama's excellence this season (+7 turnover margin is tied for 11th nationally) and prevent touchdowns even after successful drives. All in all, it points to a lower-scoring classic, where I'll favor the home team to make big plays late. With both teams 6-2 this season, the final stretch of the season, starting this Saturday, will show who's the best playoff contender . LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin walks on the sideline during the first quarter against the Kentucky Wildcats at Kroger Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect College Football Playoff hopes will be on the line Saturday. LSU and Alabama would love to notch a signature win. Alabama's opportunistic secondary could trouble Sam Leavitt and the offense. If Leavitt protects the ball and the defensive line takes advantage of a potentially vulnerable Crimson Tide offensive line, LSU should win. Tiger Stadium will be deafening, and I think the Tigers will make a statement on Saturday. LSU 35, Alabama 24 I think that the Tigers win a close one at home. This freshly healthy Alabama squad will be a tough challenge for these LSU Tigers, but I think that the LSU defense will come up with a pick-six late in the game to seal their victory. LSU 31, Alabama 28 LSU and Lane Kiffin are ready to take down Alabama. For Kiffin, he's 0-5. For LSU, a three-year losing streak will end. Sam Leavitt has made the jump and taken care of the football and looked sharp through the air, with LSU having solid o-line play to lead the way in establishing the run and attacking Alabama's defense in every way. The Tigers' defense is ready for the challenge too. With Alabama missing some key pieces on the o-line, and LSU's dominant pass rush, the matchup easily favors the Tigers. Alabama showed this against Tennessee and LSU has shown this against Ole Miss, both major opponents this season. As Saturday's matchup brings the same level of competition, it's key that both teams don't let the score turn lopsided. With the home-field advantage, I think LSU will be able to gain the momentum early, and Alabama will lose key momentum in the environment of Tiger Stadium. LSU 28, Alabama 20 While LSU vs. Alabama isn't a "storied" rivalry, it's perhaps some of the best football that gets played each year, and this matchup will be no different. Kiffin is looking for his first signature win with LSU, and if Sam Leavitt continues to play the same way he has the last two weeks, I expect it to happen. I also think that our defense is a lot stronger than theirs is; we are holding opponents to fewer points per game than their team is, despite both defenses being really good. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 12 Ohio State hosts No. 23 Oregon in a pivotal game in the Big Ten and CFP race Getty Images Week 10 of the college football season has been highlighted since the schedule was released, with No. 23 Oregon's trip to face No. 12 Ohio State among the headliners. However, when the Buckeyes host the Ducks at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS, it will not be two teams vying for a bye in the College Football Playoff, but instead two programs trying to keep their season from unraveling. The Ducks, at 5-3, have already seen their playoff dreams snuffed out, but a win last week against Northwestern brought their offense to life after a coordinator change. Dylan Raiola had his best game as a starter for Oregon in a win over Northwestern, and now the Ducks have real belief they can go into the Horseshoe and pick up a win that could salvage what's been a disappointing season. Ohio State, meanwhile, comes in with a backup quarterback of their own and is searching for answers after a 30-18 loss on the road to USC last week. Luke Fahey will get his second start and first at home, hoping to find more success and keep Ohio State in the playoff hunt after the first CFP rankings put them at No. 12 -- which would be the first team out of the 12-team playoff. The winner on Saturday will enter the stretch run of the season feeling like they've stabilized after a shock to the system in the form of losing their star quarterbacks for the year. The loser, on the other hand, will realize their goals are no longer within reach and face some hard questions entering the offseason. Where to watch Ohio State vs. Oregon live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Ohio Stadium -- Columbus, Ohio TV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com , CBS Sports App Streaming on Paramount+ Premium Ohio State vs. Oregon: Need to know Can Ohio State solve red-zone woes?: The Buckeyes moved the ball fine against USC's defense. It was the best rushing performance from Ohio State this season in Big Ten play in terms of yards per carry (4.74), and while Fahey missed some explosives, he still threw for 260 yards. The problem for Ohio State was finishing drives with six points instead of three. Ohio State made four trips into the red zone against USC and came away with just 13 points. Against Indiana , it also scored 13 points in three trips to the red zone, and the inability to come away with touchdowns nearly cost them there too. If the Buckeyes are going to control this game and keep Oregon from building belief it can win on the road, Fahey has to be sharper in the red zone and the Ohio State rushing attack has to be able to help out. Ducks find life after coordinator change: Oregon's offense had its best performance since the win at USC last Saturday afternoon against Northwestern, one week after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Interim coordinator Jay Johnson seemed able to get Raiola into a rhythm and keep him there, something the Ducks have struggled with all season (even with Dante Moore ). The frustration after the Illinois game seemed to be an unwillingness to stick with what worked -- in that game, it was the rushing attack -- and against Northwestern, once they found some concepts that worked, they went back to the well until proven otherwise. That seems simple, but it's not always easy as a play-caller to not let your mind wander and get too cute trying to stay ahead of the defense. Johnson seems more comfortable just rolling with what works and being aggressive in any spot, which seems to have a trickle-down effect on Raiola and the offense, also playing with more comfort and aggression. That's going to be necessary against an Ohio State defense that is quite good but, as USC proved, can be hit for big plays. Oregon can't be afraid to take swings as a road dog, and last week's performance gives it some confidence it can do that effectively with Raiola. Which defense can steal possessions?: With a young quarterback and a red-zone offense that's struggling, the Buckeyes might need their defense to give them a spark. For as good as the Buckeyes have been defensively this season, they haven't been great at turning teams over. They have just four interceptions on the year (94th nationally) and are 48th in total turnovers forced at 11. Raiola has been prone to turnovers for his entire career dating back to Nebraska and will likely present a couple of opportunities -- either with interceptable balls or strip sacks -- for the Buckeyes to steal a possession or two. Ohio State has to capitalize on those chances if they want to help their sputtering offense. On the other side, the best way to make Ohio State tight in this one would be to pick off the young quarterback and make Ryan Day a bit anxious about letting the young man sling it. Oregon has nine interceptions this season (13th in the country), and if they can bait the freshman into an early mistake, it could alter the Buckeyes' game plan and give the Ducks an even better opportunity on the road. Ohio State vs. Oregon prediction, picks The Ducks have to pick up where they left off offensively to have a chance here, and they should push the tempo a bit and try to stretch things out in the air. Ohio State should be able to run the ball well, and at home I would expect Fahey and the offense to operate a bit better in the red zone to put touchdowns on the board when they do move the ball. A Ducks offense trying to push it in the passing game should result in big plays (possibly for both teams), and this is a rare big game where I'm anticipating plenty of points. While people are understandably concerned about the play of Luke Fahey, Ohio State’s loss at USC last week was more on the defensive side of the ball, and Oregon has many talented players who should have Ohio State defensive coordinator Matt Patricia burning the midnight oil in preparation this week. If there is a bright spot, Oregon QB Dylan Raiola has shown a tendency to turn the ball over, so perhaps Coach Patricia will turn up the pressure to force some mistakes. away.blurb: COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State football will be thin at receiver against Oregon on Saturday, with Brandon Inniss and Brock Boyd deemed out for the matchup. Jay Timmons, who has been battling a nagging injury most of the season, was not on the injury report. The freshman defensive back is expected to be available. Offensive tackle Ian Moore, who was injured late in last week’s loss at USC and was questionable earlier this week, was not listed on the injury report. He will be available to play. The Ducks will be without running back Jordon Davison against the Buckeyes. Receiver Jeremiah McClellan is a game-time decision. The same goes for defensive tackle Eddrick Houston. He was injured late at USC and was wearing a walking boot postgame. However, he hasn’t been on any of the four injury reports this week. Kickoff for Ohio State and Oregon is slated for 3:30 p.m. ET. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. Distributed by Tribune Content Agency, LLC.

away.headline: Ohio State football's Jay Timmons trending toward return against Oregon
away.blurb: Timmons, who was held out of last week’s loss at USC with an unspecified injury, was not included on the Buckeyes’ initial availability report released for their upcoming game against the Ducks. Timmons missed games against Iowa and Maryland earlier in October before returning at Indiana when he reaggravated his injury. He traveled with the Buckeyes to Los Angeles last week as he attempted to return but was ruled out near kickoff. Wide receivers Brock Boyd and Brandon Inniss were listed as questionable for Oregon after they were held out at USC. It was the second straight game Boyd was sidelined with an unspecified injury. Left tackle Ian Moore was also listed as questionable. Moore made a late exit against the Trojans as Austin Siereveld moved over from right tackle to replace him in the fourth quarter. Defensive tackle Eddrick Houston was not listed after he went down late last week and later limped off the field at the Coliseum, indicating he could be available against Oregon. He has also practiced in recent days, prompting coach Ryan Day to express optimism about his status on Nov. 4. “We’ll have to see how the next 48 hours go,” Day said, “but he’s had two good days of practice. That would really inject a lot for us in the back end.” The Buckeyes’ secondary felt the absence of Timmons against the Trojans as they surrendered their longest passes this season between a 69-yard touchdown on the second play from scrimmage and another 70-yard reception in the third quarter. Joey Kaufman covers Ohio State football for The Columbus Dispatch. Email him at jkaufman@dispatch.com and follow him on @joeyrkaufman on X.

One major reason for the Wildcats' rise was Ohio State's loss to USC on Saturday. Kentucky is now 7-1 overall and 5-1 in SEC play, making the Wildcats one of the most surprising teams in college football this season, especially under first-year head coach Will Stein. The last time Kentucky took the field, the Wildcats defeated Vanderbilt 34-17 at home. However, they got off to a slow start, falling behind 10-0 before turning things around and taking the lead into halftime. Kentucky eventually took care of business to secure another SEC victory. Now, the Wildcats will hit the road to Knoxville this weekend to face the Tennessee Volunteers. Kentucky's most recent road game came against Oklahoma, where the Wildcats escaped Norman with a 21-13 victory. Kentucky will look to replicate that performance against Tennessee, but the Volunteers' defense has been one of the nation's best and will present a significant challenge. Tennessee Volunteers (6-2, 3-2) Tennessee has an impressive defense, but the Volunteers also have a talented running back in DeSean Bishop. Kentucky will need to find a way to slow him down, as he can make opposing defenses pay if he gets into a rhythm. Meanwhile, Tennessee's quarterback situation has been a concern, with the Volunteers relying on George MacIntyre and Faizon Brandon. The two quarterbacks have different styles. MacIntyre tends to be more conservative, often targeting receivers near or behind the line of scrimmage, while Brandon is more willing to push the ball downfield. It will be interesting to see which quarterback Tennessee turns to on Saturday against Kentucky. At wide receiver, Mike Matthews has emerged as the Volunteers' primary target, leading the team in receptions and receiving yards. Defensively, Tennessee has been impressive, recording 35 sacks, eight interceptions, and nine fumble recoveries this season. Kentucky will need to protect the football and avoid costly mistakes to have a chance to leave Knoxville with a victory. The Wildcats will likely need a near-perfect performance on both sides of the ball. Turnovers could quickly swing the momentum in Tennessee's favor, especially with the Volunteers playing in front of their home crowd at Neyland Stadium. Tennessee had an impressive 26-10 victory over Alabama at home. However, the Volunteers have also suffered a couple of notable losses, including a 20-17 defeat to Texas at home and most recently a heartbreaking 27-24 loss to South Carolina on a game-winning field goal. With both teams coming off a bye week, Kentucky will have an opportunity to prepare for Tennessee's defensive strengths. Still, winning on the road against a talented Volunteers team will be a difficult task. The Wildcats will look to keep that momentum going, improve to 8-1 overall and 6-1 in conference play, and strengthen their case for a spot in the College Football Playoff. However, the challenge does not get any easier this weekend. Kentucky must travel to Knoxville to face a Tennessee team with a dominant defense and plenty of motivation of its own. The Volunteers are also coming off a bye week and will be ready to respond after their loss to South Carolina. While Kentucky has been playing some of its best football of the season, I believe the Wildcats' winning streak comes to an end in a close, low-scoring contest. Pictured: Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop Ryan Minion · Action Network Sat, November 7, 2026 at 9:58 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kentucky Wildcats take on the Tennessee Volunteers in Knoxville, Tennessee, on Saturday, Nov. 7. Kickoff is set for 6:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Despite entering Saturday's Week 10 clash with a 7-1 overall record on the season, Kentucky remains a 6.5-point road underdog with a +188 price tag to pull off the outright upset. Tennessee is favored by 5.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -220. Kentucky is a 5.5-point underdog with a moneyline of +184. The total is set at 49.5 points (-110 / -110). Here's my Kentucky vs. Tennessee prediction and college football pick for Saturday, November 7. Kentucky vs. Tennessee Pick: Tennessee ML (-225) My Tennessee vs. Kentucky best bet is on the Volunteers to win outright. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page , and be sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Kentucky vs Tennessee Odds, Betting Line, Point Spread Kentucky vs Tennessee Spread : Kentucky +6, Tennessee -6 Kentucky vs Tennessee Over/Under : 49.5 Total Points Kentucky vs Tennessee Moneyline : Kentucky ML +170, Tennessee ML -205 In one of the bigger surprises of this college football season, the Wildcats have emerged as one of the best teams in the entire country in head coach Will Stein's first year at the helm. Kentucky senior QB Kenny Minchey has been phenomenal in his first season in Lexington after spending three years at Notre Dame and throwing the ball only 30 times there. Minchey has thrown for 1755 yards and 14 touchdowns over the Wildcats' first eight games this season with just one turnover. Freshman WR Kenny Darby has been Minchey's favorite target with over 500 yards and three touchdowns. Stein's rushing attack has been effective too, with senior tailback CJ Baxter rushing for nearly 500 yards and eight touchdowns. The Wildcat offense is averaging just shy of 33 points per game this season, but will get its most difficult test on Saturday against an elite Tennessee pass rush. Kentucky's defense has thrived under defensive coordinator Jay Bateman, who has built an aggressive, havoc -creating unit that has fared well against some elite SEC offenses this season. The Wildcats lead the SEC in interceptions and pass breakups, boasting an elite secondary led by veteran safeties Ty Bryant and Jordan Castell. While its front seven struggled early this season, Kentucky has improved drastically in the trenches over the course of the season. The 8th-ranked Wildcats are in a great spot to potentially qualify for the playoffs, but still must face several difficult conference opponents, starting with the Vols in Week 10. The 16th-ranked Volunteers put their postseason hopes on the line as Josh Heupel's bunch looks to evade a third loss this season that would very likely ruin their playoff resume. After a very promising 6-1 start to the season despite an ongoing QB battle between George MacIntyre and Faizon Brandon , Tennessee was defeated on the road at South Carolina this past weekend for the Vols' second loss of the year. Now they face a must-win game, with lingering questions about whether Heupel will stick with MacIntyre under center or return to top-ranked freshman QB Brandon. Regardless, betting markets have made their stance quite clear, with Tennessee currently listed as a near-touchdown favorite despite the Wildcats' breakout 7-1 campaign. While WR Mike Matthews has recorded over 500 receiving yards this season, Tennessee has relied far more on its rushing attack, with tailback DeSean Bishop rushing for 957 yards and 11 touchdowns, ranking sixth and ninth in all of college football, respectively. However, the Vols' defense has thrived all year, particularly at home, where it allows SEC opponents the third-fewest PPG in the conference (16.25). Jim Knowles was brought in as defensive coordinator this past offseason after serving in the same capacity for Penn State , and has significantly improved a unit that fell to 81st in the country in EPA (Expected Points Added) last season. Tennessee's defense boasts an elite linebacker corps ranked in the top 10 nationally, featuring Edwin Spillman, Amare Campbell, Arion Carter, and Jeremiah Telander. While the Vols' defense has carried this team for most of the season, especially at home in Knoxville, their offense will need to show up in this matchup, given how impressive Michey has been at avoiding turnovers. I expect this to be one of the best matchups in an absolutely loaded Week 10 slate. While I have been very impressed with the Wildcats offense and a much-improved defensive unit, I expect the atmosphere to be quite chaotic given how difficult it is for SEC foes to escape Neyland Stadium in Knoxville with an outright victory. The Vols boast an extremely dominant pass rush that should give Kentucky's offensive line fits considering how much that unit has struggled to contain elite edge pressure. That said, I feel betting markets are giving Tennessee a tad too much credit given their fragile situation at QB. In what I expect to be a pretty closely contested matchup, I'm going with the Volunteers moneyline. I got it at -210 earlier this week as soon as the line opened, and while I typically don't lay that much juice on a moneyline, especially considering the volatility of betting college football, I have confidence Tennessee gets the outright win, but laying close to a touchdown versus a red-hot Wildcat bunch is far from ideal. Though Tennessee's moneyline has since crept up to -230, I still don't mind playing the Vols at that number. Pick: Tennessee ML (-225) Check out the latest college football odds updates in VegasInsider's most recent report !

On any other Saturday, and in any other time slot, this would be the biggest game of the day, with huge SEC and CFP implications. This starts an hour before it's on, but by the second quarter, Georgia-Ole Miss and Miami-Notre Dame will both be ramping up while the Cats and Vols are humming. This will still earn a front-and-center spot, though. As good as Tennessee has been – including a relatively dominant 26-10 win over Alabama – it's coming off a 27-24 loss to South Carolina, and it's one loss away from being in a really, really tough spot to stay alive for the CFP. Kentucky got destroyed by Alabama in Week 2, but it's on a six-game winning streak. It pulled off great 35-34 wins over both LSU and South Carolina, and it won at Oklahoma. It has breathing room with just one loss, but with a rough finishing kick, beating Tennessee would be gigantic. Kentucky vs Tennessee: Quick Hits Tennessee has just one home game left after this, hosting LSU between road games at Texas A&M and Vanderbilt. Kentucky gets two of its last three games at home, hosting Florida next week and with Louisville to close, going to Missouri in between those two. Tennessee has won the last five meetings, going back to a 34-7 UK win in 2020. How To Watch Kentucky vs Tennessee Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 6:15 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Neyland Stadium, Knoxville, TN – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why Kentucky Will Win No, Kentucky isn't as talented as most of the top SEC teams, and yeah, there are a whole lot of things wrong that need tweaking. But this Wildcat team just doesn't give anyone anything to work with. Kentucky is No. 1 in the SEC in fewest penalties and No. 1 in turnover margin. The Wildcats have only been hit with 15 penalties over the last five weeks, and they haven't turned it over in any of the last four games. On the flip side, Tennessee gets flagged an average of 7.6 times per game, and while turnovers aren't a big problem, it gave the ball away eight times over the last four games. Why Tennessee Will Win Tennessee has to keep the mistakes to a minimum, and it has to keep the offense moving. It doesn't have to take any big chances against a Kentucky defense that's good against the run but doesn't do much to come up with third down stops. The Volunteer pass rush is the best in the nation, and it should be disruptive in the Kentucky backfield, but it really is about the offense. Tennessee's ground game has been fantastic – it's 16th in the nation – and that's a jumping-off point. Kentucky vs Tennessee Prediction, Betting Lines The Vols are 6-0 when the offense generates more than 320 total yards, and 0-2 when it doesn't. Only Vanderbilt and Youngstown State failed to get at least 340 yards against the Kentucky defense. Yes, Kentucky is for real. It's well coached, sharp as a tack, and it's one of those teams that just knows how to win. But with two weeks off after the South Carolina loss, the rejuvenated Vols will make a massive statement in both the SEC and College Football Playoff chases with a strong performance. picks.blurb: Tennessee football vs Kentucky picks: Vols don't lose to Wildcats in Knoxville, right? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Week 9 Winners and Losers Bears beat Bucs, barely Lakers win without Luka Puka Nacua needs MRI Knoxville News Sentinel · The Tennessean Sat, November 7, 2026 at 10:06 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Tennessee football opens a November to either remember or forget with a top-15 matchup against Kentucky on Nov. 7 at Neyland Stadium The Vols (6-2, 3-2 SEC) lost at South Carolina two weeks ago on a last-second field goal, earning a second SEC loss before the final month of the season. Kentucky (7-1, 5-1) is also coming off of an open date and has a clear path to the SEC Championship Game and the CFP. First-year coach Will Stein has molded his roster into a team that limits its mistakes and maximizes other teams' turnovers. UK has beaten Tennessee in Knoxville once since 1984, the 2020 win in front of a COVID-limited crowd at Neyland. Here are Knox News' staff predictions for Tennessee-Kentucky: Tennessee-Kentucky expert predictions Adam Sparks, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 28, Kentucky 24 The Vols can certainly beat themselves against the most disciplined team in the SEC. Kentucky leads the league in turnover margin and fewest penalties. But UT can take control of this game by winning the line of scrimmage. That means DeSean Bishop earns bruising yards and UT's defensive line collapses the pocket around Kenny Minchey. Give Tennessee the edge because of the overwhelming atmosphere of Neyland Stadium in a night game in dark mode. Emmett Siegel, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 24, Kentucky 20 The Vols still have to find something in their passing game , which is statistically the worst in the SEC. Even if that doesn't come to fruition, though, Tennessee's rushing attack and defense have been good enough to beat the toughest teams on its schedule. Perhaps the open week helped Tennessee clean up some of last game's mistakes before playing a team that doesn't make many. Playing at home could push it over the top. Cora Hall, UT beat reporter: Kentucky 27, Tennessee 24 Both teams are had a week off and are rested going into this matchup, and the Wildcats have proven they can will their way to a win when it matters. The Vols will get close, but they've been too inconsistent to bet on a win here. Stephen Thompson, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 17, Kentucky 13 I've surrendered to the idea that George MacIntyre is who he is, at least for now. But Tennessee's defense is as good as any in the country and the Neyland effect will be a difference maker in another ugly, but tight win for the Vols. Wynton Jackson, sports reporter: Tennessee 26, Kentucky 21 The Vols likely need to be perfect throughout the rest of the season to reach the College Football Playoff. Coming off the bye, that road starts with an unexpected matchup against No. 7 Kentucky. The Wildcats have solid wins, but a trip to Neyland with a national spotlight brings heightened pressure. John Adams, columnist: Tennessee 27, Kentucky 20 The Wildcats have a better record and a higher national ranking than the Vols. Moreover, Kentucky is clearly headed in the right direction under first-year coach Will Stein. But history tells us that Tennessee is always the wrong direction for Kentucky football, which has lost 38 of the previous 41 games in the series. Gentry Estes, Tennessean columnist: Tennessee 23, Kentucky 14 Props to the Wildcats on a great season, but it just feels like they are due for a letdown in a tough rivalry road game. Neyland should be jumping for this one. This article originally appeared on Knoxville News Sentinel: Tennessee football vs Kentucky picks: Vols don't lose to Wildcats in Knoxville, right?

Like last time, when top-ranked an unbeaten Clemson came to town late in the 2020 season, another ACC foe brings an unbeaten an No. 1 ranking. This time its the mighty Miami Hurricanes and the rivalry between the two programs is as strong as ever. Or does Miami leave South Bend with the No. 1 overall seed in the College Football Playoff seemingly on ice? Here's what the matchups favor on Saturday night in South Bend: When Miami Has the Ball Malachi Toney or not , this Miami offense is like few in all of college football. Sure, its biggest playmaker is out, but can Notre Dame slow down the thunder and lightning running attack of Javian Mallory and Mark Fletcher? Furthermore, Darian Mensah has 25 touchdown passes to just one interception all season long. Can Notre Dame's defense, which will be playing a bit shorthanded itself, keep Miami in check enough? That means CJ Carr's moment is now: Miami has a pass defense that has surrendered huge numbers in narrow escapes against both Florida State and North Carolina. picks.blurb: Colin Cowherd Predicts National Championship Rematch After Notre Dame Win Over Miami Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Fox Sports host Colin Cowherd is sticking with Notre Dame and Miami as his national championship pairing after the Fighting Irish handed the top-ranked Hurricanes their first loss of the season, 31-24, Saturday night in South Bend. “Nothing I saw last night changes that opinion ,” Cowherd wrote on X on Sunday morning, adding that he said before the season the two programs “would meet for the natty” and that “only Georgia is close.” Why is Cowherd still riding with Notre Dame? Fans are seen on the field after Notre Dame Fighting Irish defeated the Miami Hurricanes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cowherd backed the Irish before they played a snap. “I picked Notre Dame to win the whole thing. They’re going to be my national champion ,” he said in late August. Cowherd backed the Irish before they played a snap. “I picked Notre Dame to win the whole thing. They’re going to be my national champion ,” he said in late August. Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr held up his end of that pick Saturday, completing 29 of 40 passes for 319 yards and three touchdowns. He hit Micah Gilbert for two scores and Jordan Faison for another as the Irish built a 24-3 lead early in the third quarter. Miami pulled within a touchdown, but Notre Dame safety Luke Talich intercepted Miami quarterback Darian Mensah late in the third quarter and later broke up a potential tying touchdown pass to tight end Elija Lofton. The win mattered most for an Irish team that entered with the No. 11 College Football Playoff ranking that surprised ESPN’s Kirk Herbstreit. Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman called it “ as special of a moment , as special of an outcome that I’ve been a part of since I’ve been the head coach here.” The Irish close the regular season against Boston College, SMU and Syracuse. Malachi Toney and a Miami rematch Miami (FL) Hurricanes wide receiver Malachi Toney (1) celebrates with tight end Gavin Mueller (87) after scoring a touchdown | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cowherd attached one condition to his title game pick. “I would take the Canes in a rematch if Malachi Toney plays,” he wrote. Cowherd attached one condition to his title game pick. “I would take the Canes in a rematch if Malachi Toney plays,” he wrote. Miami wide receiver Malachi Toney suffered a high-ankle sprain in practice Wednesday and had tightrope surgery Thursday. The sophomore led the ACC with 73 catches, 1,027 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns through eight games, and CBS Sports reported he’s expected to miss four to six weeks . That timeline could put Toney back for the ACC Championship Game on Dec. 5 and keeps him on track for the playoff. His absence showed in a first half that ended with Miami trailing 17-3. Mensah then threw three second-half touchdown passes, two of them to Duke transfer Cooper Barkate. Miami finishes the regular season with home games against Duke, Virginia Tech and Boston College. The second-ranked Bulldogs backed up Cowherd’s lone exception Saturday, routing Ole Miss 42-7 as Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton threw four touchdown passes and ran for another. Georgia led 28-0 at halftime, rushed for 295 yards and snapped Ole Miss’ 16-game home winning streak . The win was Georgia head coach Kirby Smart’s first at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, and it came days after former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer named Georgia the best team in college football . The selection committee releases its second College Football Playoff rankings Tuesday at approximately 9 p.m. ET on ESPN, and Georgia has a strong case to replace Miami at No. 1. Notre Dame has ruled out linebacker Drayk Bowen, safety Tae Johnson, and cornerback DJ McKinney. Miami vs Notre Dame Over/Under pick: Over 54.5 With Mensah and Carr arguably the top two QBs in college football this season, I would play the Over at 55.5 or better , even with Toney out. South Bend will be the epicenter of the college football universe on Saturday night when the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes roll into town to face the Notre Dame Fighting Irish. We won't get to see Malachi Toney in action, but our Miami vs. Notre Dame prop picks for this heavyweight bout focus on the showdown between elite quarterbacks Darian Mensah and CJ Carr. For more college football picks and analysis, check out Rob Paul's Miami vs. Notre Dame predictions ahead of kickoff at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Nov. 7. Best Miami vs Notre Dame props Prop pick #1: CJ Carr Over 4.5 rush attempts I gave out this same prop when Notre Dame faced BYU, and CJ Carr came through. I'm backing it again, up to 55%, for many of the same reasons. It starts with the game plan. This Miami defense ranks second in EPA per rush but 110th in EPA per pass. That means we'll likely see fewer handoffs and more dropback opportunities. That also puts Carr up against a Hurricanes front that ranks 15th in pass-rush grade, per PFF, and 29th nationally in sack rate. Carr has shown this season that he's not afraid to scramble. Factor in sacks counting as rush attempts, and he should clear this total for the fifth time in seven contests. Prop pick #2: Micah Gilbert Over 31.5 receiving yards Jordan Faison leads all Notre Dame receivers with 56 targets, while Jaden Greathouse and Micah Gilbert are tied with 33 targets apiece. But Gilbert is the player being undervalued here, and I'm backing him up to 54%. Miami's secondary isn't just struggling in coverage; it's also struggling to make tackles in the open field. Gilbert has the best yards after catch per reception (5.5) of Carr's top three targets and ranks second behind Faison in yards per route run. Gilbert is also the most reliable of the three, securing 72.7% of his targets. He's averaging 70.4 receiving yards in the six games in which he's run at least 20 routes. He's a bargain with a receiving yards line that's less than half of Faison's 69.5-yard total. Prop pick #3: Darian Mensah Over 1.5 passing touchdowns With Malachi Toney sidelined, Darian Mensah has an opportunity to take another step toward the Heisman tonight, and I'm backing him up to 55% to throw multiple touchdown passes. Not only do the Hurricanes rank third in red-zone scoring, but only Notre Dame has a higher offensive Eckel rate than Miami this season. As well as Notre Dame defends, the Irish are depleted on the back end heading into this game. Defensive captain Drayk Bowen is out at linebacker, and the secondary will be without DJ McKinney and Tae Johnson. The Irish gave up three touchdown passes to UNC's Billy Edwards, one of the few quality passers they've faced this season. Mensah leads the nation in passing efficiency and completion rate, and getting him at this number is a gift. picks.blurb: College Football Playoff ranking, odds: No. 1 Miami will be historic underdog against Notre Dame on Saturday - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Week 9 Winners and Losers Bears beat Bucs, barely Lakers win without Luka Puka Nacua needs MRI Ben Fawkes Senior sports betting analyst Sat, November 7, 2026 at 3:25 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The first College Football Playoff rankings were released on Tuesday night, with Miami (FL) taking the top spot, Georgia No. 2 and one-loss Notre Dame landing outside the top 10 at No. 11 overall. The Hurricanes are No. 1 in the AP Top 25 poll as well, but will be an underdog when they go to South Bend to take on the Fighting Irish this weekend. According to Yahoo Sports research, it appears to be the first time that a team ranked No. 1 in the CFP is an underdog against a team ranked outside of the top 10. The Fighting Irish are ranked fourth in the AP poll. Notre Dame was up to a 6.5-point favorite at some sportsbooks on Thursday afternoon, but that number has moved all the way out to -8.5 because of the news that star Miami WR Malachi Toney needs ankle surgery and will miss the game . The line opened at -4.5 and had moved the Fighting Irish's direction despite the bulk of the early betting action on the Hurricanes at some books. At DraftKings Sportsbook, 75% of the wagers and 76% of the total dollars wagered are on the underdog Miami to cover the spread. "We're seeing two-way action, taking more money on Notre Dame spread and the Miami moneyline," Joey Feazel, lead college football trader at Caesars Sportsbook, told Yahoo Sports. "If I look at my current power ratings, I have Notre Dame No. 2 and Miami fifth. In the offseason, this line was closer to Notre Dame -10. Sharper action came in on the Fighting Irish early. Number feels right to me." Hurricanes QB Darian Mensah and Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith are now Heisman co-favorites at +150. Notre Dame QB CJ Carr has the third-best odds at +600, so there will plenty of movement in the Heisman market depending on how this game turns out. Toney moved from +325 to off the board. Notre Dame hosts Miami on Saturday night at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC.

picks.blurb: Film Forecast: Miami at Notre Dame- Irish Defense Preview, 11/7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Week 9 Winners and Losers Bears beat Bucs, barely Lakers win without Luka Puka Nacua needs MRI Film Forecast: Miami at Notre Dame- Irish Defense Preview, 11/7 PROVO, UT - OCTOBER 17: Preston Rex #12 of the Brigham Young Cougars is tackled by Drayk Bowen #34 and Boubacar Traore #5 of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish during the first half of their game at LaVell Edwards Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Provo, Utah. (Photo by Chris Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Justin Dottavio · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Miami Hurricanes ( 8-0 ) are headed to South Bend, IN on Saturday, November 7th to face the Notre Dame Fighting Irish ( 7-1 ) at 7:30pm on NBC/Peacock. This is the ND defense preview for the week. The 'Canes are 5th overall in SP+ while ND is 3rd . The Irish kicking game is 17th while UM's is ranked 19th . Per ESPN , ND has a 61.3 % win expectancy as 4.5 point favorites at home. ND ranks 8th in the country in SP+ Defense . The Irish scoring defense allows only 13.4 PPG which is 3rd in FBS. On the other side of the ball the Miami offense is 1st in PPG with 43.4 . Miami's offense is also 1st in SP+. On 3rd down, Miami is 2nd in the nation by converting on 55 % of their tries, and on 4th down they're only 73rd by converting on 50 % of their attempts. ND is 1st in penalty yards per game with just 28.9 while Miami is 107th at 66.4 . The 'Canes will be on the road so that won't help Mario Cristobal's bunch very much. The Irish 3rd down defense is 64th in FBS by allowing 38 % to be converted by opponent offenses. For obvious reasons I'm looking at ND's lone loss to BYU and their win over UNC. ND lost to BYU 28-24 and beat UNC 37-26 . Versus the Heels, the ND defense allowed UNC's offense to convert 6-of-11 tries on money downs. Against UNC, the ND defense held Billy Edwards Jr . to 7.5 yards per attempt with three TD's but two INT's. TE Jelani Thurman scored twice , Jordan Shipp averaged 15.6 yards per catch and the Heels rushed 3.3 yards per carry. ND finished with one sack, four TFL's and five PBU's vs. UNC's offense. UNC returned a kick 98 -yards for a TD vs. the Irish. Above- Y Cross can be a deadly play if Miami gets the time to throw it. That's one where leaving the RB in for protection (unlike Mesh and Shallow Cross) can make sense re making sure you can get the look at the deep shot on the Cross. That would've been to Toney, but now maybe Wingo? Above- One of my favorite concepts, the boot slide route to the TE, worked for UNC vs. ND. Lofton with a little jam inside before ripping out and running the slide. This goes for a TD here. Above- Miami hasn't shown power read with Darian Mensah, but it worked in spots for UNC. It doesn't have to be something you run 10x a game but 1x a half could create an explosive for a back like Mallory and slow down the ND defense. Above- The way for the defense to win wide zone it so win the outside shoulder and force it back to your slow playing LB's. The UNC back waits forever to cutback under the wave and 95 is unblocked and coming clean on the squeeze. Miami has to hit this and hit it fast. They have to use the naked boot off it, too. Above- Sure the WR is leavin' compared to the CB but remember 2-high teams will have help over the top. This ball has to be throw outside to the #'s and sideline, not inside to the #'s and hash. Above- ND's defense isn't a top-5 group just for fun. Remember the SP+ is adjusted for opponent and garbage time re their schedule. They will create some TFL's and sacks vs. the Miami OL. Here they rally fast to the screen by dissecting it better than Miami has all year. Above- More crossing routes, more success for UNC. This is a Barkate game if I've ever seen one. Miami really needs the Duke transfer to step up as a clear star. Above- Smash concept! I love smash, Miami has thrown it for a TD this year, and letting Barkate be the zig-out guy (#1 underneath) and Lofton be the corner guy could be deadly. Lofton has to show he's more than just a dude catching flat routes, though. Above- ND gets home with four, but also will use blitzes and twists to get to the QB. Up 17 with 5m to go on 4th down it's an easy time to dial up something exotic because what's the true loss? But seeing how bad Miami is vs. line games I think ND will dial them up. Above- This is the type of prowess we heard about Lofton on Greentree but haven't truly seen yet in a game. He's hurdled a couple guys but leaving a pile of wreckage he hasn't done. This could be a HUGE game for him. Against the BYU offense, ND allowed the Cougars to convert on 8-of-13 money downs. Against the Cougars ND's defense held Bear Bachmeier to 6.2 yards per attempt with one TD and one INT. Bachmeier rushed for two more scores and WR Kyler Kasper threw a TD. The Cougars rushed for 4.0 yards per carry as ND didn't log a sack. The Irish did pick up two TFL's and three PBU's with one fumble recovery. Above- Jet sweep! I love jet sweep, the ND players really saw it coming and shot the gap for a TFL. With Toney out who can be the jet guy? Wingo? Above- It's a really big shame Toney is out. BYU proved the WildCane could've been highly successful vs. ND but without Toney it may need to go to Fletcher. Above- The Digs are there. Mensah has liked the intermediate middle and it looks open vs. ND quite a bit. Above- This would be a great play to pull out but throw it back to a TE instead of Mensah the QB. I'm not sure if Barkate or anyone else can really throw the rock around but trick plays are always a way to get the boys excited and to keep them dialed in over a long season. Above- Split zone is one of my favorite run concepts. Lofton on the kick out to the right, Barkate on the '2for1' to the left. That's a slant to crack inside that takes two ND defenders with him and springs an explosive TD run. Above- Another lethal play from the WildCane pages. Fletcher at Q with Mallory as the pitchman? Maybe a swing route version with Mensah at Q and Fletcher at RB? Above- This is probably not the defense and kicking game to test the fake punt on. Stick to owning field position and forcing ND to drive 80+ Above- Y Cross is awful deadly to a healthy Toney. Maybe Upshaw, Spafford and Lofton can step up now that he's ruled out. Above- I love this Glance route inside stuff to Toney on the RPO tag. Mensah has to throw these low and inside closer to the end line or front pylons. Who can replace him with that route running ability? Maybe Barkate? The Canyonero Keys to Victory main theme from the summer was that Miami needs to win bully ball vs. Notre Dame. Like I said in the ND Offensive preview from Thursday AM I think that's changed to a shootout mentality. The individual keys for UM vs. ND are: 1- Win the turnover battle. Miami beat UNC with a strip sack. CJ Carr takes good care of the ball and has one INT just like Darian Mensah. The Irish have picked opposing QB's eight times, and have recovered eight fumbles. 2- Defend the middle of the field. While the ND TE position is less effective than usual they have four WR's getting serious action and a pair of backs that can catch the ball. Miami can't leave a massive void in the middle like they did vs. UNC. 3- Keep cooking on offense. Miami is the #1 offense in CFB, they need to stay that way vs. ND. Ryan Rodriguez has stepped up and that's a good sign vs. a nasty Irish DL. The 'Canes will need mobile Mensah against the Irish. Score Prediction: ND by 1. I think the home field advantage, Miami's weak pass defense and the Irish being a solid ball club lead to a field goal or PAT as the difference in this one.

away.headline: Malachi Toney to undergo surgery on injury, latest rumors on Miami WR's status and return timeline
away.blurb: The wide receiver started out his college career with six catches for 82 yards and a touchdown in a season-opening win against Notre Dame last year that ultimately served as a key reason the Fighting Irish missed the playoff. Notre Dame lost a key defensive player this week when green dot linebacker Drayk Bowen was ruled out with an ankle injury. The Miami Hurricanes will reportedly be tasked with defending their No. 1 ranking without their star wide receiver in the immediate future. Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reported Wednesday that Malachi Toney is "expected" to undergo surgery for the ankle injury he suffered during practice. "The current belief is that it's not a season-ending injury," Zenitz noted. The report came after Miami announced Toney "sustained an injury during Wednesday's practice and is currently undergoing further evaluation by the team's medical staff." ESPN's Pete Thamel and Max Olson first reported Wednesday that Toney is uncertain to play Saturday against No. 4 Notre Dame due to an ankle injury. Thamel noted "Toney is expected to press and attempt to play, given the magnitude of the game." The Miami Herald 's Barry Jackson reported the Hurricanes are not considering Toney's injury to be a "serious" or long-term issue, although that was before Zenitz's report. According to Jackson, a Miami coach "has told friends that he's hopeful Malachi will be back tomorrow and play Saturday." The Hurricanes and Fighting Irish are set to kick off Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET at Notre Dame Stadium. The Fighting Irish will hope to get Moore back on the field as Miami campaigns for a first-round bye and Notre Dame fights to make it back into the CFP this winter.

It was in the College Football Playoff quarterfinal at the Sugar Bowl that the Rebels ended Georgia's season with a 39-34 win thanks largely to the heroics of quarterback Trinidad Chambliss . So what will these two deliver this year? While plenty has changed from last year's teams to this year, both quarterbacks return, and there are high stakes involved here. Georgia debuted at No. 2 in the first College Football Playoff rankings of the season, and a win here would solidify their chances of reaching the SEC Championship. On the other side, the Rebels need a win to gain firmer ground. They're No. 10 in the rankings, putting them on the precipice of losing an at-large bid. Georgia vs. Ole Miss: Need to know This is the fifth straight time these two have met while ranked: Maybe that doesn't seem like something that's all that impressive to you, but for context, it had happened only five times in the first 46 meetings between the schools. Georgia has had the better end of most meetings, as they lead the series 34-14-1, and a win for Ole Miss this weekend would give the Rebels consecutive wins over the Dawgs for the first time since the 1995 and 1996 seasons. Kirby Smart has done well against ranked opponents: The Georgia coach is 44-18 against AP-ranked teams during his tenure in Athens. The last loss? To Ole Miss in the playoff last year. Trinidad Chambliss could tie a school record here: Chambliss has thrown for at least one touchdown in 21 consecutive games. If he throws one against Georgia, it will put him in a tie with former Ole Miss QB Chad Kelly for most consecutive games with a TD pass at 22. Our Staff Picks and Final Scores Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS No. 10 Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2) and No. 2 Georgia (7-1, 5-1) are set to square off on Saturday , in what will mark one of the biggest and most consequential games in the history of Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. In order to maintain control of its College Football Playoff destiny, Ole Miss will have to knock off Georgia for the third time in the program’s last four matchups. With a loss, the Rebels will put their season resume in the hands of the playoff committee with little optimism of returning to meaningful postseason play. Considering what Ole Miss has left in the final quarter of its season, there would be a lot of ground to make up. Ahead of the Rebels' top-10 matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Trinidad Chambliss and the Rebels offense was unstoppable in both matchups, particularly in Round 2, when they knocked of the Bulldogs in the College Football Playoff. This year, the calculus has changed a bit. The Rebels have a new play caller, and new weapons on the outside. The Defense has also been struggling as of late. On the other side, the Bulldogs are built on defense, running the football and controlling the clock - exactly where Ole Miss has been exploited defensively. For Ole Miss to win here, I think Chambliss - especially without Kewan Lacy in the lineup - is going to have to be Superman. We have seen him do it before plenty of times, but if the Bulldogs can deploy a similar game plan that Texas did two weeks ago, it could be a long day. Shekai Mills-Knight could be an X-factor, but it's hard to be able to rely on a redshirt freshman on a stage like this. The Rebels do have an elite home field advantage, but at the end of the day, I think it all comes down to the Rebels defense and if they can hold up against the Georgia run game. Offensively, Trinidad Chambliss will need to play a game similar to the one he played against LSU all the way back in Week 3. Like that weekend, I’m picking the Rebels to get the job done again against Georgia, but it should be much closer than the game that was last played in Oxford between these two. That should translate into a motivated team and an electric environment in Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, and when playing in The Vaught, especially at night, there isn’t a team in the country I’d take over Ole Miss. The Rebels are 26-1 at home since 2023, including a victory over the Bulldogs in the 2024 regular season that had very similar stakes as this game. Picking any team, let alone one that’s been as hot and cold as Ole Miss has been at times this season, to beat the No. 2 team in the country could age poorly. Despite that, give me Pete Golding, Trinidad Chambliss and the rest of the Ole Miss Rebels to win and keep their playoff and SEC Championship ambitions alive and send the Rebel fans home happy on Saturday night. Kirby Smart’s side will never go down easy, and Gunnar Stockton is a solid leader for the Bulldogs offense. Sparks will fly in Oxford, but a repeat of 2024 is in order. My Georgia vs. Ole Miss prediction and college football picks for tonight expect Kirby Smart's defense to rise to the occasion against Trinidad Chambliss & Co. as the Bulldogs seek revenge for last year's Sugar Bowl loss to the Rebels. Georgia is a 3.5-point favorite as it visits Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, Miss., on Saturday, Nov. 7, while the total sits at 56.5. Don't miss kickoff at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC. TOP PICK Who will win Georgia vs Ole Miss today: Georgia -3.5 Georgia and Ole Miss played two wild shootouts last year, with the Bulldogs winning the regular-season matchup and the Rebels taking it in the Sugar Bowl. This time around, I like Georgia to cover as many as 6.5 points on the road against Ole Miss. Defense will be the difference in the matchup this year, with Georgia having one of the best in the country ( ranked No. 2 by SP+ ), and Ole Miss' being one of the worst in the SEC. With the Rebels down All-American running back Kewan Lacy , the Bulldogs' defense can lock in on stopping Trinidad Chambliss . Chambliss has faced one other defense ranked top five by SP+, Texas , and struggled in a loss. Against the Longhorns, he threw three interceptions and put up a season-low 60% adjusted completion percentage. Georgia vs Ole Miss Over/Under pick: Under 56.5 Though both games between these teams last year were full of points, Georgia's defense should keep it relatively low-scoring this time around, and I would play the Under at 55.5 or better . The Bulldogs' defense ranks top 20 nationally in available yards percentage (33.5%) , havoc rate (19.4%), and success rate allowed (35.2%). With no Lacy for Ole Miss, it'll put even more on Chambliss, who has frequently had to carry the team this season, and we saw that approach fall flat against Texas. However, Georgia's offense hasn't been lighting up the scoreboard lately either, averaging just 23.6 points per game in its last three outings. So while this is one of the must-watch matchups in my Week 10 Top 25 predictions , it's not because I'm expecting another shootout. Georgia vs Ole Miss combo Ole Miss is a feast-or-famine type of team. The Rebels beat LSU and Missouri , but were blown out by Florida and fell behind so quickly against Texas that they couldn't dig themselves out. That's what happens when you lean so heavily on a star QB to make up for an inconsistent run game and one of the worst defenses in the SEC. Against Georgia, Chambliss won't be Superman; Smart has too much NFL talent on a defense that's allowed more than 20 points just once this season. If Ole Miss falls behind, Georgia's offense will lean on Gunner Stockton to manage the game and take a ball-control approach against a Rebels defense ranked 88th in the country in EPA per rush. Ole Miss team total Under 26.5 Georgia team total Over 30.5 Georgia vs Ole Miss prop: Ole Miss team total Under 26.5 Chambliss can only do so much, and against a freakishly athletic and long Georgia defense, I don't think Ole Miss will be scoring at nearly as high a clip as it has against lesser SEC teams. I would take the Under on Ole Miss' team total at 24.5 or better . Georgia linebacker Chris Cole is arguably the best defensive player in the country, and Glenn Schumann and Kirby Smart could deploy him as a Chambliss stopper. With 4.5 40-yard dash speed and nearly 34-inch arms, Cole has earned his nickname of "Tarantula." Look for the Bulldogs to spy Chambliss with him and use him as a blitzer too; he leads Georgia in pressures (24) and pass-rush win rate (17.4%). With Cole hunting Chambliss and the Bulldogs' defense ranking top 20 in rush success rate (37.8%), Ole Miss will struggle to find the end zone. away.blurb: Isiah Canion was one of Georgia's biggest acquisitions out of the Transfer Portal this offseason. He came to Georgia after spending two seasons at Georgia Tech, and he was expected to be a central piece of the Bulldogs' passing attack this year. He unfortunately was hurt during the second game of Georgia's season and hasn't seen the field since. Earlier this week though he was marked probable to play on Georgia's official injury report and on Thursday he was nowhere to be found on their report which means he has been officially cleared to play. This injury update does need to be taken with a grain of salt. Nate Frazier came off Georgia's injury report heading into the Alabama game, but he still didn't play. Based on that it still isn't a 100 percent guarantee that Canion will play against Ole Miss, but he most likely will be available. Chauncey Bowens still questionable to play vs Ole Miss While it looks like Georgia will finally be getting Canion back, the same can't be said for running back Chauncey Bowens. On Thursday's injury report he was still listed as questionable to play, so there is a chance he will be able to suit up against the Rebels. There however is just as good of a chance that he won't be able to play either. Another injury report will come out Friday night before one final injury update about an hour before kickoff on Saturday. Georgia's injured 3-headed monster could all return in time to play Florida Georgia WR Isiah Canion injury update is great news for UGA Canion has only recorded three receptions for 28 yards this season. That can't be held against him though because the starters barely played in Georgia's season opener against Tennessee State before he got hurt the following week in Week 2. Canion has a lot of potential though that Georgia hasn't seen yet. Last year at Georgia Tech he was an integral part of their talented offense as he recorded 33 receptions for 480 yards and four touchdowns. He isn't a player that will ever be the No. 1 target in Georgia's offense, but he can be another reliable option for Gunner Stockton in a game where UGA needs a lot of offense. This is great timing for Georgia because the Ole Miss offense, with quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, dominated UGA the two times they played last season. Georgia's offense likely needs to score a lot of points to win this game, and Canion being back on the field will help them accomplish that. away.source: Dawn of the Dawg on MSN
away.blurb: Arguably Georgia's biggest game of the season is against Ole Miss, and that matchup has finally arrived. The Bulldogs are looking for some revenge after the Rebels knocked them out of the playoff last season, but on top of that they are hoping to strengthen their hold on the SEC with a win this weekend. Georgia has gotten a lot of great injury news heading into their matchup with Ole Miss. Wide receiver Isiah Canion has been out since the second game of the season, but on Thursday he was removed from their injury report and appears to be making his return this weekend. Running back Chauncey Bowens could also be making his return this weekend as well. He was injured a few weeks ago and when it initially happened some people in the program feared it could've been season ending, He hasn't been fully cleared to play against Ole Miss yet, but on Friday he was listed as probable to play on their official injury report. Ole Miss on the other hand isn't getting as lucky on their injury report. Star running back Kewan Lacy will miss his second game in a row this weekend after being hurt at Texas. EDGE Kam Franklin and linebacker Keaton Thomas are game-time decisions for Ole Miss, but if either player is ruled out that would be difficult for the Rebels to overcome. So much is on the line for both teams this weekend, so here is all the information fans need to know to watch. What time do Ole Miss and Georgia play? Kickoff between Ole Miss and Georgia is scheduled for 7:30 pm EST on Saturday, Nov. 7. This game is being played in Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, MS. How to watch Ole Miss and Georgia Georgia and Ole Miss will air on ABC. This game can also be streamed on Fubo TV and the ESPN app as well. The spread for nearly every college football game will shift at some point throughout the week from where it originally opened. That however didn't happen with this matchup. Georgia originally opened as a three point favorite over Ole Miss, and as of now they are favored by 3.5 points over the Rebels. Georgia is 6-2 against the spread so far this season. Ole Miss on the other hand is only 4-4 against the spread this year. The Rebels are much better against the spread at home against top 15 teams though. Over the past four years they are a perfect 6-0 at home against the spread and straight up against top 15 teams which includes their 28-10 win over Georgia in 2024. So while the odds are in Georgia's favor heading into this game, history shows that Ole Miss stands a great chance at winning this game. They are nowhere near becoming a traditional rivalry, but the last few years they have met multiple times with so much on the line each time they've played. home.blurb: Arguably Georgia's biggest game of the season is against Ole Miss, and that matchup has finally arrived. The Bulldogs are looking for some revenge after the Rebels knocked them out of the playoff last season, but on top of that they are hoping to strengthen their hold on the SEC with a win this weekend. Georgia has gotten a lot of great injury news heading into their matchup with Ole Miss. Wide receiver Isiah Canion has been out since the second game of the season, but on Thursday he was removed from their injury report and appears to be making his return this weekend. Running back Chauncey Bowens could also be making his return this weekend as well. He was injured a few weeks ago and when it initially happened some people in the program feared it could've been season ending, He hasn't been fully cleared to play against Ole Miss yet, but on Friday he was listed as probable to play on their official injury report. Ole Miss on the other hand isn't getting as lucky on their injury report. Star running back Kewan Lacy will miss his second game in a row this weekend after being hurt at Texas. EDGE Kam Franklin and linebacker Keaton Thomas are game-time decisions for Ole Miss, but if either player is ruled out that would be difficult for the Rebels to overcome. So much is on the line for both teams this weekend, so here is all the information fans need to know to watch. What time do Ole Miss and Georgia play? Kickoff between Ole Miss and Georgia is scheduled for 7:30 pm EST on Saturday, Nov. 7. This game is being played in Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, MS. How to watch Ole Miss and Georgia Georgia and Ole Miss will air on ABC. This game can also be streamed on Fubo TV and the ESPN app as well. The spread for nearly every college football game will shift at some point throughout the week from where it originally opened. That however didn't happen with this matchup. Georgia originally opened as a three point favorite over Ole Miss, and as of now they are favored by 3.5 points over the Rebels. Georgia is 6-2 against the spread so far this season. Ole Miss on the other hand is only 4-4 against the spread this year. The Rebels are much better against the spread at home against top 15 teams though. Over the past four years they are a perfect 6-0 at home against the spread and straight up against top 15 teams which includes their 28-10 win over Georgia in 2024. So while the odds are in Georgia's favor heading into this game, history shows that Ole Miss stands a great chance at winning this game. They are nowhere near becoming a traditional rivalry, but the last few years they have met multiple times with so much on the line each time they've played. Next up for Jon Sumrall and Co. are the Oklahoma Sooners, who travel to Ben Hill Griffin Stadium in Week 10 for the first-ever meeting between the two schools as mutual members of the Southeastern Confernece. They have met twice before — both times in the postseason — including the 2009 BCS Championship game, in which the Orange and Blue prevailed for their second national title in three years. This season, Florida (5-3, 3-3 SEC) sits just outside of the US LMB Coaches Poll top 25 and just barely hanging on in the AP Top 25 at No. 25, while Oklahoma arrives in Gainesville voteless in both major polls with a 4-4 record (2-3 SEC).
