picks.headline: Sooners Wire Staff Predictions for Oklahoma vs. Florida
picks.blurb: Sooners Wire Staff Predictions for Oklahoma vs. Florida - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Week 9 Winners and Losers Bears beat Bucs, barely Lakers win without Luka Puka Nacua needs MRI Sooners Wire Staff Predictions for Oklahoma vs. Florida Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oklahoma Sooners are heading down to Gainesville, Fla., for the first time ever to take on the Florida Gators . The Sooners need to win two of their final four to earn bowl eligibility . With a new voice leading the offense, the Sooners are hoping for a turnaround to end the 2026 season. Jason Witten takes over an offense that has underachieved this season, given the number of returning starters along the offensive line and the weapons at returning quarterback John Mateer. How much better can Oklahoma be in a week is the question on everyone's minds. It's unlikely the Sooners will suddenly erupt on offense, but if they find more consistency, they'll have a chance to finish the season on a high note. So how will the Sooners perform in "The Swamp?" Our staff here at Sooners Wire picked this week's showdown between the Sooners and the Gators. Too Many Questions Oklahoma tight ends coach Jason Witten, left, talks with coach Brent Venables during a Sooners football spring practice in Norman, Okla., Thursday, April 9, 2026. There are just too many moving parts for Oklahoma to reliably believe the Sooners could win a road game in the swamp. The Sooners have made a change at offensive coordinator and the availability of a bunch of notable players on both sides of the ball are still in question. There's also the question of how Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer will play without Ben Arbuckle on the sideline for the first time in years. Even though Florida has a few issues to worry about as well, they're certainly not as dire as Oklahoma's at the moment. Florida 21, Oklahoma 10 James D. Jackson, Contributor Improved Sooners Touchdowns? Touchdowns. Oklahoma made a huge move this week by letting go of Ben Arbuckle and having Jason Witten call plays. Witten called plays as a high school head coach and had a ton of success doing it. I think the offense will play with a fire we haven't seen this year, and the defense will return to its dominant ways. Because of that, I've got OU winning and the offense scoring three touchdowns. OU 27, Florida 17 Oklahoma 27, Florida 17 Jaron Spor, Contributor Defense gives Oklahoma a chance Sep 4, 2026; Norman, Oklahoma, USA; UTEP Miners quarterback EJ Colson Jr. (1) throws as Oklahoma Sooners defensive lineman David Stone (0) chases during the game at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Last week's disaster set in motion a sequence of events that should end with Brent Venables' team having a new offensive coaching staff, a new starting QB, and new faces up and down the offensive depth chart. For now, though, the only change is the absence of OC Ben Arbuckle, so all of Oklahoma's other offensive problems remain. Expect OU's defense to bounce back against Florida, but expect the offense to continue faltering for the remainder of this season. Florida 16, Oklahoma 7 Aaron Gelvin, Contributor Promising, but Sooners struggle Oct 31, 2026; Norman, Oklahoma, USA; Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) throws during the first quarter against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. picks.blurb: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Week 9 Winners and Losers Bears beat Bucs, barely Lakers win without Luka Puka Nacua needs MRI Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? Oklahoma Sooners tight ends coach Jason Witten will take over as interim offensive coordinator for the rest of the season. | Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Chapman · Oklahoma Sooners On SI Fri, November 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Gators have an impressive resume, having beaten No. 4 Ole Miss 52-28 at The Swamp, then going on the road to Austin and taking down No. 7 Texas 27-24 - one week after OU beat them in Dallas - on a night the underwhelming Florida defense overwhelmed Arch Manning and the Longhorns, sacking him five times, limiting UT to 2-of-10 on third down (they had 13 first downs total) and holding the Horns to 272 total yards. But they were also blown out in back-to-back losses to No. 25 Missouri and unranked South Carolina, which preceded last week's 27-8 loss to No. 3 Georgia. Oklahoma is a touchdown underdog to Florida, but the Sooners are the best defense the Gators face. Still, OU may be reeling after its worst defensive performance in years in the blowout loss to South Carolina - which included an incomprehensible 25 missed tackles (usually 10 is a bad number). OU's first trip to The Swamp will be punctuated by another big game from Gators RB Jaden Baugh, who's third in the SEC at 100.3 rushing yards per game and first with 13 rushing TDs. Final score: Florida 28, Oklahoma 21 Things could get gross Saturday night. Florida has officially made a quarterback change, and Tramell Jones Jr. could be without a pair of key weapons to pair with an already banged up offensive line. Oklahoma's offense has been so bad it got its coordinator fired, but Jason Witten has never called plays collegiately and John Mateer is still likely the quarterback the Sooners will roll with. OU's defense needs to bounce back after its tackling struggles last week, but even an improved showing could see Gator running back Jaden Baugh have enough success to push Jon Sumrall's team across the finish line. Final: Florida 16, Oklahoma 13 OU is set up for further disaster as it heads to the swamp. Jason Witten will serve as the Sooners' play caller for the first time at the college level, John Mateer is still the quarterback and Ben Hill Griffin Stadium is one of the nation's most hostile atmospheres. But amid the weirdness, I expect OU to win this game. Teams often come out more inspired after a notable firing, and I predict Witten will lead a creative game plan as he auditions for the full-time offensive coordinator role. Florida's offense is good - but it is also prone to turning the ball over. If the Sooners are able to put pressure on Tramell Jones Jr. early, it will create a long day for the Gators' offense. Final: Oklahoma 24, Florida 20 The Sooners figure to get a little boost from Jason Witten's playcalling, but don't expect massive changes in either scheme or production here. The offensive line still has its issues, John Mateer hasn't been consistent at all, and neither of the other quarterbacks have experience in games like this. But Oklahoma's defense does figure to have a bounce-back game after struggling to contain LaNorris Sellers and the South Carolina offense. The tackling will be better, and Florida's offense is in a bit of flux itself with Tramell Jones Jr. expected to make his second start of the season at quarterback and Florida's offensive line struggling in recent weeks. But the Gators still have plenty of talent, especially on the offensive side, and The Swamp is one of the toughest environments in college football. That's a tough position for a reeling team to be placed in. The game will be close into the second half but the Gators figure to pull away and hand Oklahoma its second consecutive defeat. Final: Florida 24, Oklahoma 14 Brady Trantham A new offensive coordinator doesn'tchange the fact that John Mateer is still QB1 at OU. Mateer gives Oklahoma their best shot in any game, but in 20 games as the Sooner signal caller, it is apparent that he simply isn't very good. A coaching change can, in theory, help him in spots, but if OU needs their QB to make a play in a tight game, chances are he will make that play - just for the other team. Florida sticks to the run and gets Oklahoma on a few explosives and rides it to an easy win. Pete Fiutak · College Football News Sat, November 7, 2026 at 2:18 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads When we last saw Oklahoma and Florida play, the Sooners rolled 55-20 in the 2020 Cotton Bowl over a high-powered Gator team that lost to eventual national champion Alabama in an epic SEC Championship. The other meeting was the BCS Championship at the end of the 2009 season, when Tim Tebow and the Gator defense took down Heisman-winner Sam Bradford and the amazing Sooner attack 24-14 for the national title. The stakes aren't as high this time around, but for a Florida program that's on the rise, and No. 24 in the first College Football Playoff rankings, and for a 4-4 Oklahoma desperate to close strong, this will be intense. Oklahoma vs Florida: Quick Hits Oklahoma at 4-4, needs to win two of its last four to be bowl eligible. It hosts Ole Miss and Texas A&M after this before closing at Missouri. Florida is coming off the 27-8 loss to Georgia. It goes to Kentucky next, hosts Vanderbilt, and finishes at Florida State. Again, the first two meetings were in big bowl games. This is the first regular season matchup between the two. How To Watch Oklahoma vs Florida Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 7:45 PM ET TV: SEC Network Location: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville, FL – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why Oklahoma Will Win The defense continues to fight the good fight. It had a problem in the 42-25 loss to South Carolina, but the defense is fantastic on third downs thanks to a pass rush that takes over games. But to beat Florida, you have to slow down the run. The Gators are 0-3 when running for fewer than 155 yards, and the Sooners give up just 107 yards per game. Only Mississippi State and, last week, South Carolina have been able to gash the Sooners for more. Why Florida Will Win Oklahoma's offense has a hard time running the ball. With a defense as good as the Sooners have, all the O has to do is keep it moving and not screw it up. But no running game means more pressing overall, and then come the mistakes. The Sooners only average 107 yards per game on the ground, and they just can't find any room to move. The Gators have to hold up, and then pounce on an Oklahoma attack that turned it over four times against both Georgia and Kentucky, three times against New Mexico, and twice against Michigan. Oklahoma vs Florida Prediction, Betting Lines It's stupid, but if you buy into these things, going back to the last two games of last season, Oklahoma is on a ten-game run of alternating wins and losses. The Sooners beat Texas, then lost to Kentucky, beat Mississippi State, lost to South Carolina, beat … Florida? The Sooners have the defense to hold up and make Florida struggle. The Gators got by Texas a few weeks ago, but it's been a struggle, losing three of the last four. Weird trends aside, this Oklahoma team really does have a way of rallying when it absolutely has to. away.blurb: Off a disappointing loss to Georgia, the Florida Gators (5-3, 3-3 SEC) return home to face Oklahoma (4-4. 2-3 SEC) at The Swamp on Saturday, November 7 (7:45 p.m., SEC Network). The 6-0, 196-pound Jones is 1-0 as a starter, leading Florida o a 27-24 upset win at Texas on October 17 when Philo was out with a shoulder injury. The Gators will be down one starter on the line as right tackle Emeka Ugorji has been ruled out for the Oklahoma game. That opens up an opportunity for 6-8, 319-pound right tackle Caden Jones, who made 10 starts for the Gators last season. Florida will face a challenge against an Oklahoma defense that ranks fifth in the SEC sacks (23) and seventh in tackles for loss (6.1). The Gators will look to get star running back Jadan Baugh back going, as the 6-1, 225-pound Baugh has failed to rush for more than 100 yards in four straight games. The return of Duke Clark, who has been out close to a month due to injury, also could help spark the run game. "We've been trusting each other a lot better than what we have in the past. I feel like in the past, everybody was playing out of sync almost in a way," Florida defensive lineman Brendan Bett said. "But these last few games, I think we kind of just locked arms and just really trusted each other to compete and execute and do our jobs at an elite level." Florida will honor Hall of Fame coach Urban Meyer during the game, inducting him into the stadium's ring of honor. Meyer was involved in the process to hire Sumrall, who is trying to get the Gators back on track after a 1-3 October that included the 27-8 loss to the Bulldogs on Halloween in Atlanta. "Not what we need to do last Saturday as a team," Sumrall said. "We got an opportunity to respond this week, excited about that. A lot of growth is needed within our football team. We're hard at working, getting it done." Here are five storylines to watch in UF's matchup with the Sooners: Can Florida football QB Tramell Jones Jr. provide a spark to the offense? Florida is turning to Jones as starting quarterback after incumbent starter Aaron Philo threw two interceptions and was benched in the first half against Georgia. Jones was able to move the offense in relief of Jones against the Bulldogs, passing for 172 yards and rushing for 17 yards and a TD. "Attribute that to a lot of poise, right, and preparation," Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner said. "He knows where everybody he is. There's probably a couple we'd like back, but other than that I thought he did a good job. Got to continue to work, continue to get better." For the season, Jones has passed for 579 yards and 4 TDS while throwing 3 interceptions. He's also added 83 yards and 1 TD rushing. Can Florida football OL raise its level of play to protect Jones and get the run game back going? It's a real injury that we thought we were on the other side of that he had a setback last week, and it sucks. I mean, it freaking sucks for him." Oklahoma has eight players who are not expected to play on Saturday: linebacker Taylor Heim, defensive back Dakoda Fields, wide receiver Trell Harris, linebacker Cole Sullivan, tight end Trynae Washington, defensive back Jacobe Johnson, and offensive linemen Ryan Fodje and Fred Hinton. home.headline: Scouting report, prediction as Florida football hosts Oklahoma
home.blurb: Off a disappointing loss to Georgia, the Florida Gators (5-3, 3-3 SEC) return home to face Oklahoma (4-4. 2-3 SEC) at The Swamp on Saturday, November 7 (7:45 p.m., SEC Network). The 6-0, 196-pound Jones is 1-0 as a starter, leading Florida o a 27-24 upset win at Texas on October 17 when Philo was out with a shoulder injury. The Gators will be down one starter on the line as right tackle Emeka Ugorji has been ruled out for the Oklahoma game. That opens up an opportunity for 6-8, 319-pound right tackle Caden Jones, who made 10 starts for the Gators last season. Florida will face a challenge against an Oklahoma defense that ranks fifth in the SEC sacks (23) and seventh in tackles for loss (6.1). The Gators will look to get star running back Jadan Baugh back going, as the 6-1, 225-pound Baugh has failed to rush for more than 100 yards in four straight games. The return of Duke Clark, who has been out close to a month due to injury, also could help spark the run game. "We've been trusting each other a lot better than what we have in the past. I feel like in the past, everybody was playing out of sync almost in a way," Florida defensive lineman Brendan Bett said. "But these last few games, I think we kind of just locked arms and just really trusted each other to compete and execute and do our jobs at an elite level." Florida will honor Hall of Fame coach Urban Meyer during the game, inducting him into the stadium's ring of honor. Meyer was involved in the process to hire Sumrall, who is trying to get the Gators back on track after a 1-3 October that included the 27-8 loss to the Bulldogs on Halloween in Atlanta. "Not what we need to do last Saturday as a team," Sumrall said. "We got an opportunity to respond this week, excited about that. A lot of growth is needed within our football team. We're hard at working, getting it done." Here are five storylines to watch in UF's matchup with the Sooners: Can Florida football QB Tramell Jones Jr. provide a spark to the offense? Florida is turning to Jones as starting quarterback after incumbent starter Aaron Philo threw two interceptions and was benched in the first half against Georgia. Jones was able to move the offense in relief of Jones against the Bulldogs, passing for 172 yards and rushing for 17 yards and a TD. "Attribute that to a lot of poise, right, and preparation," Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner said. "He knows where everybody he is. There's probably a couple we'd like back, but other than that I thought he did a good job. Got to continue to work, continue to get better." For the season, Jones has passed for 579 yards and 4 TDS while throwing 3 interceptions. He's also added 83 yards and 1 TD rushing. Can Florida football OL raise its level of play to protect Jones and get the run game back going? home.blurb: Oklahoma vs. Florida injury report: Who's out and who has to step up for the Sooners Skip to main content Recruiting Starting center Jake Maikkula was removed from the availability report after missing last week against South Carolina. Left tackle Michael Fasusi is also still healthy since his return two weeks ago. That leaves OU without only Ryan Fodje, who will miss his third game in a row. The Sooners also got good news on the defensive side of the ball, with cornerback Eli Bowen set to return after missing the last four games. S Peyton Bowen: GAME-TIME DECISION Safety Peyton Bowen was also listed on the injury report last week before ultimately being available against South Carolina. Hopefully, it's the same conclusion this week but he's even healthier, because Bowen is a vital piece of OU's defense as one of 15 semifinalists for the Jim Thorpe Award, which goes to the best defensive back in college football. Replacement: If Bowen can't go, Michael Boganowski should get the start after also starting last week, even with Bowen available. Florida's QB play won't be as good, but Boganowski made some early mistakes against South Carolina, so the Sooners need Bowen out there. OL Eddy Pierre-Louis: GAME-TIME DECISION Offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis hasn't seen the field since Week 4 against Georgia because of an injury. It looks like he will miss another one on Saturday, meaning he's officially been out more games than he's played this season after starting at guard the first three weeks. Wide receiver Elijah Thomas, who was listed as probable on Friday, will make his return after missing the past two games. He's caught five passes for 49 yards this season. ILB Jaden Robinson: out OL Emeka Ugorji: out TE Evan Chieca: out DL Jeramiah McCloud: out WR Vernell Brown III: out It's been a week of change for the Oklahoma Sooners, including players actually getting healthier instead of getting worse on the availability report. Newly appointed interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten will get the rare occurrence in Norman of having nearly his entire starting offensive line healthy for his play-calling debut against No. 24 Florida on Saturday night. That alone should have OU's offense looking better after Ben Arbuckle was fired on Monday. OU, though, can still never go a week without a lengthy injured list.
